To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the histology curriculum at the School of Medical Sciences at the University at Albany, State University of New York (SUNY) was reformed by reducing contact time in the laboratory; and (2) the histology laboratory course was restructured so that half of all laboratory work that had been performed with a histology microscope was now performed with computer applications.

1) the computer‐assisted histology laboratories are more efficient than traditional microscope exercises, 2) the computer‐based exercises are more effective in teaching histology than traditional microscope exercises and, 3) the computer‐aided histology laboratories are a valuable component of a laboratory course in histopathology.

(1) the use of interactive computer applications to teach histology is an effective instructional strategy, (2) computer applications can replace some microscope exercises in a histology laboratory course without reducing the effectiveness of the course, and (3) computer applications can be integrated into a histology course in such a manner that the course can accommodate curricular reform.
